summary: Unexpected OAuth consent prompts after opening prospect CSV DOCX — possible phishing consent flow
description:
Issue summary: Multiple employees reported seeing OAuth consent prompts requesting access to 'View and manage Google Drive files' and 'Manage service accounts' after downloading a DOCX attachment labeled 'Q2 Prospect List' from a cold outreach email. Users who clicked the link were routed to an external consent page that pretended to be our IdP.

Impact: Potential unauthorized consent grants and ephemeral tokens issued that could be used to enumerate service accounts and read linked Drive files. At least two users approved the prompt before being stopped by security. No confirmed data exfiltration found in the first 48 hours, but suspicious API calls were observed from two employee sessions.

Environment: Prod SSO (Okta) federated to GCP and Google Workspace. Affected users primarily in us-west office; cross-org emails originate from external vendor domain.

Observed behaviour: After opening the DOCX, users reported a browser popup requesting they "Sign in with Redwood" and then an OAuth consent screen for a third-party app named "Marketing Asset Importer" requesting elevated scopes. The consent screen used our logo and a subdomain that looked similar to our IdP. Two users granted consent.

Expected behaviour: Downloading internal prospect lists should not trigger any OAuth consent flows. Legitimate Salesforce/marketing integrations are pre-approved and use our internal app registry.

Initial evidence:
- Okta system log IDs: okta-log-55512, okta-log-55513
- Google Workspace OAuth audit entries: gw-oauth-20260310-01, gw-oauth-20260310-02
- Affected users: j.diaz@redwood.ai, m.ross@redwood.ai (redacted in ticket)

Recommended immediate actions already taken:
- Reached out to users and instructed them not to interact further with the file/link.
- Blocked the sender domain at gateway and quarantined the original email.
- Revoked the two recently issued OAuth tokens via Google admin console.
- Initiated short-term conditional access policy to require re-auth for web OAuth requests from unknown subdomains.
steps_to_reproduce: Receive cold outreach email with DOCX attachment 'Q2 Prospect List'
Download and open DOCX in browser or Word—document contains a visible link labeled 'Import to Drive'
Clicking the link opens a browser tab pointing to hxxps://drive-import.redwood-verify[.]com/oauth?app=marketing
Consent page displays Redwood branding and asks for Google Workspace and service account scopes
If user approves, OAuth grant is recorded in Google OAuth audit logs and tokens are issued
logs: SIEM alert: siem.alerts#84721 - anomalous oauth_grant events
comments: Aisha Patel (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed two teammates saw a consent page after opening a doc from an unfamiliar vendor. Raised immediately via #security-alerts.
Marcus Liu (Assignee) - 2026-03-10: Began triage; blocked sender, quarantined messages, revoked suspicious tokens. Need SSO logs and affected account list.

Lena Cho (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Observed two unusual API calls to projects/infra-monitoring from j.diaz session after the OAuth grant. Calls were limited to read-only storage listing, no writes detected. Collecting full request headers.
DevOps Vendor (external) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed domain in question is malicious and is part of a phishing kit. Provided takedown request template.
CISO (Evelyn Park) - 2026-03-11: Approve user-scoped token revocations and organization-wide short-lived token policy. Notify legal if any PII access found.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:12 UTC - Triage started. Identified OAuth grants with app name 'Marketing Asset Importer' created 2026-03-10 09:58 UTC.

Browser forensics: the DOCX contains a link to hxxps://drive-import.redwood-verify[.]com/oauth which resolves to 198.51.100.42 (malicious host). The subdomain includes our company name to add legitimacy.

Okta logs show an external redirect to hxxps://auth.redwood-verify[.]com that is not in our IdP app registry. No SAML assertions from our IdP were generated for these events—this was a direct OAuth page to Google.

Google OAuth audit shows scopes granted: openid, email, profile, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloudplatform.readonly (service account token exchange scope).
Affected assets: two user tokens revoked; audit of Drive files accessed shows read operations on a shared marketing folder by IPs 203.0.113.27 and 198.51.100.42, both external and not on allowlist.
No evidence of data exfil beyond listing and metadata reads. Investigating whether service account exchange requests succeeded—pending GCP audit logs retrieval.

Cross-references: related to INT-70319 (repeated-token-exchange-requests-from-geo-diverse-ips) for similar token-exchange pattern observed previously. Also flagged under phishing campaign cluster in SIEM (cluster id phish-202603).

Containment: blocked malicious host at perimeter, applied URL block in user agents, added domain to organization-wide denylist. Notified legal and compliance to prepare customer notification checklist if PII access is confirmed.
resolution: Revoked all OAuth grants associated with 'Marketing Asset Importer' and forcibly rotated refresh tokens for the two affected users. Blocked the phishing domains at perimeter and engaged hosting provider for takedown of 198.51.100.42. Implemented a temporary IdP policy requiring Okta MFA for any new OAuth consent that requests high-privilege scopes and blocked user-initiated service-account scope grants. Delivered company-wide advisory about the specific phishing lure and added an automated inspection to email gateway that flags DOCX files with external OAuth links. Follow-ups: schedule a tabletop with Support/SRE/IR to update runbook and add automated OAuth grant anomaly alerting to SIEM.
